text:
A muscle fibre relaxes when it stops receiving nerve impulses, so acetylcholine is cleared from the neuromuscular junction (broken down by acetylcholinesterase) and the fibre is no longer excited. Calcium is then actively pumped back into the sarcoplasmic reticulum, and tropomyosin re-blocks the myosin-binding sites on actin. The question is cut off after "when:", so this assumes the standard textbook answer.
